summary: The project is an interactive web experience that documents the history of space equipment abandoned by NASA, such as the Ranger modules. It addresses the "Discarded but Not Forgotten" challenge by transforming technical data and historical missions into accessible, visual narratives. This is crucial for inspiring new generations, preserving the legacy of exploration, and fostering an interest in space science.
details:
My project is an interactive educational website. It functions by documenting and narrating the history of the Ranger mission, transforming technical data into accessible narratives. Its benefits include educating the public and raising awareness about space exploration, thereby inspiring new generations. The intended impact is to foster an interest in science and document a historical legacy. The tools used include Eleven Labs, Gemini,pinterest, ChatGPT, Canva, Wikipedia, NASA Space Apps, Pixverse Video, Vidnoz Gen, Deepvid AI, CapCut, TikTok, YouTube, Google Translate, TikTok Downloader, Replit, Unlimited TTS, WCAG guidelines, and GitHub. The development was carried out using languages ​​such as HTML, CSS, and React. The project is creative in that it incorporates scientific research on voice preferences and personalized narratives, while also considering factors like font size, colorimetry, and color psychology to ensure accessibility and readability.

"Although factors such as font size, colorimetry, and color psychology were considered to ensure accessibility, their implementation was limited by technical constraints; consequently, the focus remained primarily on the narrative and the integration of voice and imagery, subject to availability."
